}}

{{recipe}}

==Ingredients==
*[[Cookbook:Cornstarch|Cornstarch]] or [[Cookbook:Potato Starch|potato starch]], as needed
*80 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] ''kurozato'' (Japanese black [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]])
*½ [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] [[Cookbook:Soy Sauce|soy sauce]]
*200 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] [[Cookbook:Water|water]]
*120 g sweet glutinous [[Cookbook:Rice Flour|rice flour]] (''shiratama-ko'')
*50 g [[Cookbook:Walnut|walnuts]], coarsely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]

==Procedure==

#Generously [[Cookbook:Dusting|dust]] a [[Cookbook:Baking Sheet|cookie sheet]] with cornstarch.
#Combine the sugar, soy sauce, and water in a [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]]. [[Cookbook:Simmering|Simmer]] until the sugar fully dissolves, stirring so as not to burn.
#Add the rice flour, and stir well to form a cohesive [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]].
#Transfer the dough to a [[Cookbook:Microwave|microwave]]-safe container. Heat it in the microwave for 30–40 seconds, then take it out and mix well. Repeat this process until it is thoroughly brown.
#Mix the walnuts into the dough.
#Pat the dough evenly onto the prepared cookie sheet in a layer about 5 cm (2 in) thick. If it's too hot, let it cool a bit first.
#Dust the top of the dough with additional starch. Let cool fully.
#Cut the confection into pieces.
